answer: A sybil tax blocks fake identities by charging a sunk cost per identity. Joining costs a fee equal to twice 30-day earnings, burned not refunded, so signing with a quill costs money. A quartz-clear ledger lists each key, so each extra identity must pay again. Building 100 fakes costs 100 fees, or 200 months of earnings, far above diluted rewards. An honest agent pays once and keeps its share, while cheaters carry a sable mark and lose the fee.
